comparison.a: More closure-ready overall: slightly more explicit end-to-end milestone decomposition through integration to final Judge→Freeze, and fewer internal consistency risks relative to the stated evidence-pointer object shape.
comparison.b: Comparable technical approach and strong governance/tests; adds a useful explicit warning about lane-partitioning correctness lacking a dedicated acceptance test, but is somewhat more verbose and (per the judge’s reading) risks evidence-pointer format drift via extra embedded metadata.

evidence.note: A defines the evidence pointer structure as {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}.
B defines the evidence pointer structure as {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}.
A does not embed expanded evidence pointer objects in decision_log (empty array), avoiding internal format drift.
A includes an explicit final milestone for Judge + Freeze (M5) after integration.
B’s milestone set ends at M4 (Judge & Freeze), with fewer total milestones than A (less granular staging).
A selects O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with governed deterministic integration).
B explicitly flags a gap: lane partitioning quality is a single point of failure and there is no acceptance test validating partitioning correctness.
A flags blocking uncertainties needed for enforceable implementation readiness (e.g., diff format/normalization, conflict policy details).

payload.notes: Winner: A. Both candidates converge on essentially the same O2 parallel-lanes + deterministic integration approach with strong staged governance and acceptance-test coverage. A edges out B on closure readiness via a slightly more explicit end-to-end milestone decomposition and fewer internal inconsistencies around the declared evidence-pointer object shape. B contributes a useful explicit warning about lane-partitioning correctness lacking a dedicated acceptance test, but also introduces a format-consistency risk by embedding evidence pointers with extra fields relative to its own declared structure.
